bio.text: Tim Griffin, a Republican, has been Attorney General of Arkansas since January 10, 2023, and is seeking re-election in 2026.
He was Arkansas's lieutenant governor from 2015 to 2023 and represented Arkansas's 2nd Congressional District in the U.S. House from 2011 to 2015.
Griffin has served in the U.S. Army Reserve Judge Advocate General's Corps for more than 26 years, holds the rank of colonel, and served in Mosul, Iraq, in 2005.
He graduated from Hendrix College and Tulane Law School and lives in Little Rock.
